S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any death, serious injury, fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal event presenting a material risk to the regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material risk to their unit or requires immediate customer action; other material safety notices must be sent promptly and no later than 10 business days after confirmation.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. Manufacturers shall submit complete per-model results to the regulator. Results need not be published publicly by individual company or model, but customers considering or owning a specific model must receive that model’s test results, including its failure rate. A model exceeding the 5% failure-rate benchmark must be reported to the regulator, with a corrective-action and retesting plan. Exceeding the benchmark alone shall not automatically prohibit sale: the regulator shall set a reasonable, risk-based compliance period and interim safeguards, considering test results and incident data, before deciding on restrictions.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed home battery systems must support remote emergency shut-off. For units already installed that lack this capability, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent compliant upgrade within six years of this standard’s effective date.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard’s adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers and regulators of a material safety defect, provide interim risk-reduction instructions, and explain available remedies. A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period; the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers and implement the regulator-approved recall and remedy.

document.section_notes: S1 is weakened because it covers only serious/material-risk events rather than all thermal incidents, though its deadlines are tight. S2 is weakened because the 5% benchmark does not automatically stop sales; the regulator can set an open-ended compliance period with no numeric interim cap, and per-model results go to purchasers/regulators but not the public. S3/S4/S5 are largely acceptable: six-year retrofit, 36-month built-in suppression, and a mandatory 8-per-100,000 recall with prompt notice, though S5 is strict for Halcyon (Ember 8 at 9.9/100k) and has no phase-in.
